**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 78
**Title (English, from literature):** Not ordaining a trainee who has followed one

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Anubandha-sikkhamānana-vuṭṭhāpana-sikkhāpada* is the seventy-eighth rule in the *Pācittiya* section of the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga*. The rule addresses the conduct of a nun who promises to ordain a female trainee (*sikkhamānā*) on the condition that she attends upon her for two years; if the nun subsequently makes no effort to confer full ordination or arrange for her ordination, she incurs an offense that must be confessed (*pācittiya*). An English translation of the rule has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

Curated parallels across canonical traditions demonstrate the broad transmission of this monastic precept, with corresponding rules appearing in the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Pācittiya 78) and *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (Pācittiya 78), as well as in the Vinayas of the Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahāsāṅghika, and Lokottaravāda traditions preserved in Chinese, Tibetan, and Sanskrit. Automated text-reuse analysis confirms this cross-traditional continuity, finding significant alignment with the Sanskrit *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* [DharmaNexus].
